subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: What identity authority should OpenClaw expose as trusted inbound sender metadata for agent routing and private-message decisions?
rationale: Current code intentionally keeps sender names and per-turn ids out of trusted system metadata, so adding this field changes a model-visible security, privacy, and prompt-cache boundary rather than filling a purely mechanical omission.

options.title: Use Configured Principals
options.body: Expose a trusted principal only when a stable provider ID matches an operator-configured identity link, while keeping display names in untrusted context.

options.title: Use Stable Provider IDs
options.body: Expose stable provider IDs as trusted metadata and require agents or tools to resolve human-readable names outside the prompt contract.

options.title: Use Resolved Display Names
options.body: Expose platform-resolved display names directly, accepting the higher privacy and spoofing-review burden for easier agent ergonomics.

recommendation.title: Use Configured Principals
recommendation.body: Expose a trusted principal only when a stable provider ID matches an operator-configured identity link, while keeping display names in untrusted context.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the trusted/untrusted prompt boundary and adjacent sender-spoofing fixes points to steipete.
